As I read the second section of 4(A), I believe that he needs prior written approval from the Developer. “No improvements or change of any kind, including without limitation any (e) construction placement of or addition to or alteration of any: (ii)walkways, driveways, parking area; shall be commenced or permitted to remain on any lot unless such improvement or change has the prior written approval of Developer.” He then has to get approval from the city too.

subject: Landings HOA Status and some updates
bodyText:
Fellow Landings HOA Board members,

        As some of you may know, I am currently the HOA Treasurer. Also that I missed this year's homeowners meeting, which was a simple mistake on my part, having inadvertently entered the time of the meeting for 4:00 PM instead of 1:00 PM. It was kind of embarrassing, especially since I had prepared a financial report, which I was supposed to give (fortunately I had given it to Jesse, who presented it to you all, I presume). :<) :<)

        Now back to the present. I retrieved some documents that came in the mail to our accountants (WRP on Upper Gilchrist Road). I sent them to Jesse since I thought he was still the Board president. I was surprised to find out he is not. So I'm a little embarrassed again to admit that I seem to be in the dark.

Was a new president elected at the February meeting?
Are we still going to continue as an HOA?

I see emails from time to time that seem to indicate we still have an interest as a group in deed restriction issues (driveways, for example). But nothing more in the way of planned meetings to discuss these issues or the status of the dam, etc. (We used to have regular meetings when Jeff Harris was president.)

Anyway, I would hate to see the HOA die with a whimper. I know there are issues that need to be addressed, specifically deed restrictions concerning solar panels that could be updated if we summoned the will and the energy. I don't think we should give up. It will be much harder to restart than to continue, and make changes if necessary.

OK, next topic. What follows is the email I sent to Jesse. It describes the documents that came to our accountant, which I now have in my possession and can share with anyone who would like copies. I don't think they require any action on our part, but I thought you should know what is going on.

Also, I have been Treasurer for three years, which I think is the unofficial reasonable time to be a Board officer. I am willing to continue as a Board member, but would like to relinquish the Treasurer duties no later than next year's Homeowners meeting (Feb 2023). It's really an easy job, since we employ an accouningt firm (WRP CPAs) who do all of the record-keeping, check-writing, auditing, taxes, etc. Basically all you have to do is check the mailbox at PakMail once or twice a month, and carry important papers (like bank statements and bills) from PakMail up to WRP on Upper Gilchrist road. And keep copies of all of the documents in a nice neat folder or notebook. Easy-peasy. I really have to quit for certain reasons and hope that someone will step up sooner than later.

Here is what I sent to Jesse:

Jesse,

        Hope you're enjoying your summer!

        Number one, our accountants WRP CPAs received two (copies of) legal notices, one from Frost, Brown, and Todd containing "A Report on Landings Plats" from the Knox County Common Pleas Court of the original planning maps for all Landings development phases. It appears to be merely an addendum with no other documentation about how it might be used in court.

        Number two, another Knox County Common Pleas Court document (copy) from Fischer, Evans, and Robbins, Ltd. declaring that Waters Edge Homeowners Assoc. Inc. has new legal counsel, namely from Fischer, Evans, and Robbins, Ltd. Don't know how that affects us, but anyway, there it is. Just as an aside, there are about 6 legal firms mentioned together with a host of other important entities and individuals listed as recipients. Must be a lot of money to spread around somewhere!!

        Did you receive these yourself? If not I can make copies, if you wish.

        Number three, as you know, this is my third year as Treasurer. I would like to be replaced no later than next year's homeowners' meeting in February. So I thought we should start looking for a candidate now. It never works to "nominate" some unwilling and unsuspecting candidate on the spot. Any ideas? I am really serious about this, so I want to get a head start.

Cheers,
Mike

subject: The short version:  Landings HOA Status and some updates
bodyText:
HOA Board members:

        Since I have not heard a peep from anybody concerning my last email, I will assume it is because it was too long and discouraged all of you from reading far enough to reach my main points. So I will try to be brief here:

1. For various personal reasons, I would like to resign as treasurer of the Landings HOA effective no later than the Homeowners' annual meeting next February. I have performed the duties for three years now, and it's time for someone else to step up.
2. This leads to the larger issue, which is, do we still have a viable HOA Board, or even an overall HOA, period? Again I apologize that I missed this year's meeting (last February) due to my inadvertently entering the meeting time 3 hours late in my calendar.
3. I have not been able to determine if we have a new president or not, or even if there is a common will to continue the HOA. Therefore, I am uncertain how to proceed. Of course I would like to be replaced in an orderly fashion according to the HOA covenants.
4. But if the majority has no interest in maintaining the HOA, and is just waiting for it to die (which I think is a bad idea), I don't want to be left in the position of being the last person responsible for the money that is left in the HOA bank accounts.

Can anyone enlighten me on whether we have a new president, intend to continue as an HOA, and finally whether I can be replaced in an orderly fashion as treasurer?

Sincerely,
Mike Ulrey

subject: Re: The short version:  Landings HOA Status and some updates
bodyText:
Hi Mike -

At the last annual meeting, it was my impression that there was a stronger voice supporting maintaining the HOA than those asking for it to be disbanded.

Regarding your role as treasurer, I completely understand your desire to resign. I think we should consider who would want to be considered for that role. Mike, I would take any recommendations that you might have there.

With regards to solar panels, I am happy to draft an amendment that would allow for them. However, I am not going to determine the recommended requirements. It is my understanding that broadly allowing solar panels is not what the neighbors would approve, but something with more restrictions would be more palatable by them. I do not have the background or the strong interest to take on determining the requirements of solar panels that the HOA would consider. I’m also happy to notarize signatures.

Cynthia A. Cunningham, Esq.

subject: FW: The short version: Landings HOA Status and some updates
bodyText:
To all:

          I appreciate some of you responding. At least I know someone is out there! :<) :<)

          However, my concern is one level down from specific issues (such as solar panel approval) for now. Since Jesse quit and no meetings have occurred, and I can’t even seem to find out if a new president was elected, I’m not sure how we will even function. Certainly no decisions will be made as a group via sporadic email exchanges among a few participants.

          I want to see the HOA board continue, but I also want to find a new Treasurer. I will need some structure to work within that I cannot seem to find at the moment. I am somewhat uncomfortable being the only Board “officer” at the moment (till someone tells me differently). If I am going to find someone to replace me, it would certainly help if we had a meeting to find out who is still involved and interested, to get ideas, and to reassure me that there is still an organization with a beating heart, so to speak. I just feel like the HOA interest has greatly shifted underneath me, and I will be the last one with official responsibility, which I don’t want at this point, for as I said, some personal circumstances.

Sincerely,
Mike

subject: Landings HOA Status
bodyText:
Dear HOA Board members (and a couple of others):

        Last July, I informed you that I would like for someone else to step up and serve as Treasurer of our HOA. (Note: I do not mean to say it has to be a Board member. There might be a likely candidate among the HOA as a whole. I personally don't know of anyone, but maybe one of you does.) It is coming up on my 4th anniversary as Treasurer, and I would like to step down.

        I have not been given any direction on how to proceed (except for isolated private conversations). In fact it seems like there is an unspoken wish for the HOA to simply disappear.

        It that is the case, I want to let you know the consequences if I quit without any replacement, and to ask what you think I should do about it.

1. We have roughly $7800 in our combined savings/checking account with Park National Bank. What should I do to make this money "safe" until it is decided "officially" if you want to continue or not? I have asked our accountant WRP to advise me on this.
2. The HOA Board insurance will not be paid. Therefore, anyone on the Board will be personally liable for any costs related to lawsuits brought against the Board.
3. The PakMail mailbox bill will not be paid, so we will no longer receive mail, bills. etc.
4. The accountant WRP will not be paid, so someone else will have to write checks, interface with the bank, audit the books, and submit the appropriate tax forms (we don't owe any taxes but are required to certify our nonprofit status every April).
5. The city lot next to the pond (bordering Woodlake Trail) will not be mowed (unless someone does it for free or is paid "under the table"), creating an eyesore, at least for those proximate to the lot.

   In addition, in the broader view, our covenants require an "all homeowners" meeting in February. This will have legal consequences if we simply ignore it. We need to make it official one way or the other about continuing as an HOA.

        One last item. Given the difficulty of resolving this via random email exchanges, I am willing to host a meeting at my house for the HOA Board members to discuss further, if you wish. Sometime before the end of the year, if possible.

   Sincerely,
   Mike Ulrey
   Treasurer Landings Phase VII and VIII HOA

subject: RE: Landings HOA Status
bodyText:
To all:

                Based on the responses I have received, I propose a homeowners board meeting on Sunday Nov 13 2022 at 1:00 PM. It will be a hybrid meeting, so as to accommodate Nuh (who is in Algeria on sabbatical). You are welcome to attend in person at my house (4 Longvue Ct) or login to the Zoom meeting.
Please let me know whether you will attend in person or by Zoom so I can plan accordingly.

          I envision the topics to be:

  1. How to gauge the sentiment of the HOA at large (beyond just the Board) on whether to continue the HOA or not. (At required Feb 2023 meeting?)
  2. Assuming a positive answer, we need to elect new board officers, such as president, VP, secretary, and treasurer. (Not on Sunday, but sometime in the future.) As far as I can tell, the treasurer (that would be me) is the only one left.
  3. What to do if the majority opinion is to disband. We need to read and understand the Covenants to determine how to do this legally. We should also consider consequences, for example, relative to:

     * HOA funds still in the bank
     * HOA board liability insurance
     * Whether to retain an accountant
     * Tax reporting (again we don’t owe any, but we must declare our non-profit status each year)
     * If and how we retain someone to mow the city lot next to the dam
     * And yes, will it change anything relative to the still-pending dam issue, legally speaking? (we will need expert advice on this one from the lawyer types).

  1. Bring your own questions or comments.

Thanks,
Mike Ulrey
4 Longvue Ct
740-501-3701
